chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, who said:

I performed Hajj with my father, and with me was a sister of mine. So when we arrived in Makkah, she menstruated, and she panicked with an intense panic, fearing that the Hajj would be missed by her. So my father said to me, 'Go to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and say to him that my father conveys the greeting to you, and says to you that a young girl of mine, whom I am performing Hajj with, has menstruated and panicked with an intense panic, fearing that the Hajj would be missed by her. So what are your orders for her?'
He said, 'So I went to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he was in the Sacred Masjid. So I stood by his side. So when he looked at me, he gestured to me. So I went to him and said to him,

He said, 'So I returned to my father and conveyed it to him. He said, 'So he instructed her with that, and she did so, and the blood was cut off from her, and she fulfilled all of the rituals. So when she departed from Makkah after the Hajj, and came to be in the carriage, the blood returned to her.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ): Abu Al-Hasan (AS), referring to Imam Al-Hasan (AS)
key_terms.فَلْتَسْتَدْخِلْهَا: Let her insert it inside (her body)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for a woman who menstruates during Hajj and wants to complete her rituals?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *istidkhal* (internal tamponade) using milk-soaked cotton, a practical juristic solution to ensure the validity of Hajj rituals despite menstruation. It highlights the Imam’s authority in providing specific medical-legal remedies that allow a pilgrim to perform all rites, emphasizing the Shia scholarly focus on facilitating religious obligations through tangible means. The narrative underscores the importance of timely action and the specific conditions under which menstruation is considered to have ceased for ritual purity purposes.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammam, or someone else, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from his brother Al Husayn who said,

‘I performed Hajj with my father, and with was a sister of mine. So when we proceeded to Makkah, she menstruated, and she panicked with an intense panic, fearing that she would miss the Hajj So my father said to me, ‘Go to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and say to him<sup>asws</sup> that my father conveys the greeting, and is saying to you<sup>asws</sup> that a young girl of mine who I am performing Hajj with has menstruated and panicked with an intense panic, fearing that she would lose the Hajj. So what are your<sup>asws</sup> orders for her?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the Sacred Masjid. So I paused by his<sup>asws</sup> side. So when he looked at me, gestured to me. So I went over to him and said to him, ‘My father conveys the greetings to you<sup>asws</sup>’, and I repeated to him<sup>asws</sup> what my father had instructed me with. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Deliver the greetings to him, and tell him to instruct her to take some cotton with water of the milk, so let her enter it inside her. So the blood would cut off from her and she can fulfil her rituals, all of them’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So, I left to go to my father, and repeated it to him. So he instructed her with that, and she did so, and the blood was cut off from her, and she fulfilled the rituals, all of them. So when she left from Makkah after the Hajj, and came to be in the carriage, the blood returned to her’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad or others from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother, al- Husayn who has said the following:

“I performed al-Hajj and my father and sister were with me. When we arrived in Makkah she began to experience Hayd (menses). She strongly regretted for fear of losing her al-Hajj. My father told me to see abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and say to him, ‘My father sends you his greeting of peace, and says that my young daughter with whom I have come for al-Hajj is experiencing Hayd (menses) and she is strongly mournful about it for fear of losing her al-Hajj. What is your instruction?’

I went to see abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) was in Masjid al-Haram. I stood in front of him (the Imam). When he saw me he made a gesture. I went to him and said that my father sends him (the Imam) his greeting of peace. Then I conveyed my father’s message. He (the Imam) said, ‘Say my Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) and tell him to ask her to take a piece of cotton with water from milk and place it inside. Her bleeding will stop and she can perform all of her acts for al- Hajj.’

I returned to my father and conveyed the instruction. He instructed her accordingly and her bleeding stopped. She attended all places for performing acts of al-Hajj. When she left Makkah after al-Hajj and sat in the carriage on camel-back, bleeding commenced.’”
